"The unexamined life is not worth living." - Socrates

*beep beep beep beep, beep beep beep beep*
The shrill, relentless beeps of an alarm shattered the silence in the gray-shrouded bedroom. A form stirred on the bed, pulling the blankets tightly around to shield themselves from the noise. Several minutes passed before they couldn't bear it any longer. With a sudden motion, an arm shot out to deliver a brutal slap to the sound source, finally silencing it. It was a familiar morning routine, apparently someone from this house prevented him from rotting in bed and being forgotten by the world, as he sincerely wished.

The form on the disheveled bed shifted, and a 18-year-old boy with messy hair emerged from the depths of the blanket. His name was Andy, a teenage boy looking like no other, but what sets him apart from others is an inexplicable air surrounding him, and a pair of eyes as dark as the deepest abyss. Yanking the bedroom curtains open, the chill of the cloudy autumn morning greeted him as he looked out on the busy streets. At a neighboring park next to their apartment, he saw three preschool children playing hopscotch. Upon the sight of the scene, he remembered that he used to love playing it with other children. In his very blurred memory, they would compete to see who could jump all the boxes faster, but to him now, it seemed pretty silly. He also saw the street cleaning volunteer, a retired yet cheerful and healthy-looking old man going on his way to sweep fallen leaves. Such a noble act would be admired by other passerbys, with some of them pausing on their way to work to chat with him. To Andy, it appeared to be a futile attempt to relieve themselves of the guilt from some long-forgotten misdeed.
reply: That alarm story is wild. I prefer the quiet of stone over beeping.
